answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: every agent stakes a small bond that unlocks only after a long voyage of honest work, like a slow climb from a knoll at dawn. Each attestation is a step upward, each fraud a fall back to the start. New accounts begin untrusted, so a thousand fake identities cost a thousand bonds and a thousand dawns, while one real agent compounds trust instead.
